clue.text: Vegetable matter a domestic animal has eaten

indicators.note: something eaten is taken inside, so the animal word swallows the letter

parts.note: a pet is an animal kept in the home

explanation.surface: A household pet has gobbled up some plant matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Peat is partly decomposed plant material dug from bogs, so it is literally vegetable matter.

clue.text: Explosive females at matches in Scottish isles

parts.note: HE is the standard abbreviation for high explosive
a match is a marriage, and the women being married at weddings are brides

explanation.surface: Fiery women at sporting fixtures somewhere off the west of Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matches' looks sporting, but here it means weddings.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrides are the island chain off Scotland's west coast, so they are a group of Scottish isles.

clue.text: Endless task given to a learner associated with singing

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter of the task word is dropped

parts.note: a chore is a routine task
L is the learner driver's plate letter

explanation.surface: A never-ending job handed to a student connected with singing lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' drops the final E of CHORE, leaving CHOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Choral describes music for a choir, so it is an adjective meaning connected with singing.

clue.text: Placed side by side with group opposing

parts.note: a set is a group of things belonging together
against means in opposition to

explanation.surface: Seated next to a faction that is hostile to you.
explanation.definitionFit: To set one thing against another is to compare it by juxtaposition, placing the two side by side.

clue.text: Susan's bowled over by the legendary hero

indicators.note: knocked over, so the letters are tipped the other way round

parts.note: Sue is short for Susan, so Susan's becomes Sue's

explanation.surface: Susan is overwhelmed by a mythical champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowled over' reverses the shortened name; Sue is the usual short form of Susan.
explanation.definitionFit: Theseus is the Greek mythological figure who slew the Minotaur, a classic legendary hero.

clue.text: Guy providing drinks with energy

parts.note: teas are hot drinks
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A man serving beverages with plenty of vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' is a verb here, meaning to mock, not a man.
explanation.definitionFit: To guy someone is to make fun of them, which is a synonym of teasing them.

clue.text: Circuit material making comedic turn so dreadful

indicators.note: something dreadful is in a terrible state, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: An electronics part that makes a comedy routine awful.
explanation.definitionFit: Silicon and similar semiconducting substances are the material from which electronic circuits and chips are built.

clue.text: Baddies in car first to escape

indicators.note: the opening letter gets away, so it is removed

parts.note: wheels is slang for a car

explanation.surface: Villains in a getaway vehicle, the leader making a run for it.
explanation.walkthrough: In wrestling a heel is the villain, so heels are baddies.
explanation.definitionFit: A heel is slang for a contemptible person or a wrestling villain, so heels are baddies.

clue.text: Foot of water in cathedral office

indicators.note: the water word sits inside the office word

parts.note: a see is a bishop's office or seat, centred on a cathedral
a pond is a body of water

explanation.surface: A measure of water found in a church building's office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foot' is a metrical foot in poetry, not a body part or length.
explanation.definitionFit: A spondee is a metrical foot of two stressed syllables in verse.

clue.text: Daughter getting behind, being less sensible

parts.note: after means behind in sequence

explanation.surface: A girl falling behind and becoming sillier.
explanation.definitionFit: Daft means silly, so its comparative form is the opposite of more sensible.

clue.text: Map's original creator with new layout

definitions.text: Map's original creator with new layout

indicators.note: the original part of a word is its opening letter
the letters of the word are given a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The man behind the famous map, with the world laid out afresh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new layout' rearranges the word creator, after the first letter of 'Map's'. Read whole, the clue also describes the cartographer himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Gerardus Mercator devised the projection that gave world maps a new layout, so he is the creator of that map.

clue.text: I am clothed afresh and well-organised

indicators.note: done again in a new way, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone getting dressed again in an orderly way.
explanation.definitionFit: Methodical means following a systematic method, which is a synonym of being orderly.

clue.text: Shrubs faring badly in ashy garden

indicators.note: doing poorly, so the letters end up in a mess

explanation.surface: Bushes struggling in a dusty, ash-strewn plot.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydrangeas are flowering garden bushes, an example of shrubs.

clue.text: Man readily available when husband is away

indicators.note: absent, so that letter is removed from the word

parts.note: handy means close at hand and convenient

explanation.surface: A man who is always around when the woman's husband has gone out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' is the definition: Andy is simply a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Andy is a common male first name, so it can stand for a man in crossword fashion.

clue.text: Nomad is drunk outside a meeting-place somewhere in New York

indicators.note: intoxicated, so these letters are reeling about

parts.note: the article a, standing outside, after the rearranged letters
a venue is a place where people meet

explanation.surface: A tipsy wanderer standing outside a gathering spot in Manhattan.
explanation.definitionFit: Madison Avenue is a street in Manhattan known for advertising, so it is a location in the city.

clue.text: Poet and playwright heard in town by Thames

indicators.note: spoken, so the word sounds like the town name

parts.note: Marlow is a town on the River Thames in Buckinghamshire

explanation.surface: A literary figure listened to in a riverside town.
explanation.walkthrough: MARLOW is a town on the Thames in Buckinghamshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Marlowe wrote Doctor Faustus and also the lyric poem The Passionate Shepherd, so he was both.

clue.text: Unusual blue lava worth a lot

indicators.note: out of the ordinary, so the letters are set in an odd order

explanation.surface: Strangely coloured volcanic rock that fetches a high price.
explanation.definitionFit: Something valuable has great monetary worth, which matches being worth a lot.

clue.text: Smaller beast that shines in the night

definitions.text: Smaller beast that shines in the night

parts.words: Smaller beast that shines in the night
parts.note: the Little Bear constellation, whose stars glow in the night sky

explanation.definitionFit: The Latin constellation name means Lesser Bear, a smaller beast made of stars visible after dark.

clue.text: Quick rhythm evident in gavotte!

parts.note: a faster tempo, punning on the doubled T visible in the dance name

explanation.walkthrough: The joke: GAVOTTE shows a double T, and a gavotte is a dance with a musical time.
explanation.definitionFit: Double time is a musical tempo twice as fast, hence a quick rhythm.

clue.text: European man losing head when grabbed by pretty girl?

indicators.note: the shortened word is seized and held inside the girl word

parts.note: dish is slang for an attractive person

indicators.note: the first letter is cut off

parts.note: taken as the word man

explanation.surface: A beheaded fellow being caught by an attractive young woman from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing head' cuts the first letter from man, and 'when grabbed by' holds what is left inside the slang word for a pretty girl.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dane is a native of Denmark, a European nation, so the nationality adjective names a European.

clue.text: See 16
Party that's horrible with teachers' group providing something to eat

parts.note: a do is a party
ugh is the exclamation of disgust
NUT is the National Union of Teachers, a British trade union

explanation.surface: A dreadful bash with schoolteachers' union members serving the food.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUT was the National Union of Teachers in the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: A doughnut is a fried ring or ball of sweet dough, a snack to eat.

clue.text: Like an understudy on stage?

definitions.meaning: temporarily standing in for someone, as a deputy does
performing a role in a play

explanation.definitionFit: An understudy is a temporary stand-in, an interim deputy; and performers in a play are doing theatre work.

clue.text: Pipe from bath taking last of waste

parts.note: a tub is a bath

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A drainpipe leading from a bathtub to carry off dirty water.
explanation.definitionFit: A tube is a hollow cylinder for conveying fluid, a synonym of a pipe.

clue.text: Archaeologist taking vehicles to edge of site

indicators.note: the edge here is the final letter of the word

parts.note: vans are vehicles

explanation.surface: A dig leader driving trucks to the perimeter of an excavation.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Arthur Evans excavated Knossos in Crete.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Arthur Evans was the British excavator of Knossos, a famous archaeologist.

clue.text: Car slightly deficient facing ban — this could strengthen its frame

indicators.note: a little short, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: Rolls is short for a Rolls-Royce car
to bar is to ban

explanation.surface: A luxury car falling short of a prohibition, then a safety part for its chassis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slightly deficient' drops the S of ROLLS; 'its' refers back to the car.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll bar is a metal bar over a vehicle's cabin reinforcing its structure against overturning.
